question: Drugs causing hypokalemia are : a) Amphotericin B b) Insulin c) Cyclosporine d) Carbenoxolone e) NSAIDs
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Carbenoxolone" -> "enhanced renal sodium reabsorption" -> "secondary increase in potassium excretion" -> "hypokalemia" -> 90%
CHAIN: "NSAIDs" -> "reduced renal blood flow" -> "reduced potassium excretion" -> "unlikely to cause hypokalemia" -> 30%
analysis: Option opa (ace) is selected as it includes Amphotericin B, Insulin, and Carbenoxolone, all of which are known to cause hypokalemia through well-understood mechanisms. Cyclosporine's direct link to hypokalemia is less certain, and NSAIDs typically cause hyperkalemia, supporting the exclusion of these drugs from the correct answer.
